stage: independent initial inspection; no candidate reviewed
independence: Inspected the source snapshot, fixed target, style-only family concept and asset records directly. Did not read other object aesthetic reviews, editor proposals or candidate rationale.
sourceObservations: The source reads as a blue L-shaped wall cap over amber horizontal wood bands. The open inner corner and the long horizontal and returning portions identify the modular corner.
The blue cap is a nearly uniform, flat saturated area. Its planes have little visible depth or edge roll, and the inside bend is a sharp, graphic notch.
The wood reads as broad rectangular bands with straight narrow dark separators. Its lower area becomes considerably darker; the surfaces have little crafted material information or rounded volume.
At the 192 by 352 logical frame the silhouette and palette are clear, but the large blue surface and wood bands look comparatively spare and hard-edged.
targetObservations: The fixed target makes the blue cap visibly rounded and substantial, with a broad blue top plane, darker blue side depth, and softened outer and inner edges.
Warm amber wood gains separate rounded planes, warm edge light and restrained broad grain. The cap and wood feel more deliberately made.
At logical size the stronger volume and warm/cool separation survive. Large highlights are more useful than the fine grain lines.

The target has a bright, nearly white rim and a diagonal crease across the blue bend. These are aesthetic information, not required geometry; avoid copying a sharp crease, halo or overly glossy edge if it harms soft cartoon cohesion.
The target is internally larger and differently placed than the source on its canvas. Its apparent silhouette extent and placement cannot define the production footprint or registration.
The family-concept image supports the same blue-cap/amber-wood treatment and soft edge volume. It is style-only evidence and does not establish the corner form or exact straight-wall settings.

rankedDesiredOutcomes.outcome: Make the corner feel like a coherent, softly rounded native construction, with readable blue cap thickness and an intentional inside turn, while retaining its open L clearance and matching join profiles.
Bring warm wood and clear blue material separation into the existing palette family, with broad soft highlights, readable warm wood bands and no large dead dark surfaces in any facing.

Use purposeful crafted detail and improved surface/edge forms that remain visible at logical size, then prove the corner belongs to a continuous wall in native and independently assembled sprite joins.

immutableConstraints.registration: Actual orthographic camera and pixel aspect from source-camera.json; logical frame 192x352, root [96,256], one-world-unit/128-logical-pixel cell, native frame 384x704 at sourceScale 2. No view fitting, image warping or camera-facing reference card.
immutableConstraints.geometryAndFunction: One-cell footprint, functional height 1.02, L path, concave opening/clearance, occupied envelope, W and N connection planes, cross-sections, handedness and material bands preserved through actual N/E/S/W rotations.
immutableConstraints.family: Use the approved wall-middle family settings when supplied. Native and sprite connection continuity is required, not inferred from a lone corner image.
immutableConstraints.capture: Static one-frame clip, all four actual native rotations, transparent RGBA, no directional ground shadow and no preferred horizontal lighting direction.

modelingFreedom: Original part counts, blank surfaces and awkward nonfunctional geometry are not constraints. Reward useful changes to native forms, structure and decoration away from locked joins and clearance.
limitsAndPendingEvidence: Only one original snapshot and one fixed aesthetic target view are supplied. No unseen reference view is invented; future views must be coherent with the same object and family.
